paragraphs.text: The Healthy Habits Survey shows that only about one third of American seniors have correct habits. Here are some findings and expert advice. 1. How many times did you brush your teeth yesterday? Finding: A full 33% of seniors brush their teeth only once a day. Step: Remove the 300 types of bacteria in your mouth each morning with a battery-operated toothbrush. Brush gently for 2 minutes, at least twice a day. 2. How many times did you wash your hands or bathe yesterday? Finding: Seniors, on average, bathe fewer than 3 days a week. And nearly 30% wash their hands only 4 times a day—half of the number doctors recommend. Step: We touch our faces around 3,000 times a day—often inviting germs to enter our mouth, nose, and eyes. Use toilet paper to avoid touching the door handle. And, most important, wash your hands often with hot running water and soap for 20 seconds. 3. How often do you think about fighting germs? Finding: Seniors are not fighting germs as well as they should. Step: Be aware of germs. Do you know that it is not your toilet but your kitchen sponge that can carry more germs than anything else? To kill these germs, keep your sponge in the microwave for 10 seconds.

Using too much water or throwing rubbish into our rivers are clear ways that humans can put our water supply in danger, but we are also affecting our water supply in less obvious ways. You may wonder how paving a road can lead to less usable fresh water. A major part of water we use every day is groundwater. Groundwater does not come from lakes or rivers. It comes from underground. The more roads and parking lots we pave, the less water can flow into the ground to become groundwater. Human activity is not responsible for all water shortages. Drier climates are of course more likely to have droughts than areas with more rainfall, but in any case, good management can help to make sure there is enough water to meet our basic needs. Thinking about the way we use water every day can make a big difference, too. In the United States, a family of four can use 1.5 tons of water a day! This shows how much we depend on water to live, but there's a lot we can do to lower the number. You can take steps to save water in your home. To start with, use the same glass for your drinking water all day. Wash it only once a day. Run your dishwasher only when it is full. Help your parents fix any leaks in your home. You can even help to keep our water supply clean by recycling batteries instead of throwing them away.

When 19-year-old Sophia Giorgi said she was thinking of volunteering to help the Make-A-Wish Foundation, nobody understood what she was talking about. But Sophia knew just how important Make-A-Wish could be because this special organization had helped to make a dream come true for one of her best friends. We were interested in finding out more, so we went along to meet Sophia and listen to what she had to say. Sophia told us that Make-A-Wish is a worldwide organization that started in the United States in 1980. It's a charity that helps children who have got very serious illnesses. Make-A-Wish helps children feel happy even though they are sick, by making their wishes and dreams come true, Sophia explained. We asked Sophia how Make-A-Wish had first started. She said it had all begun with a very sick young boy called Chris, who had been dreaming for a long time of becoming a policeman. Sophia said lots of people had wanted to find a way to make Chris's dream come true—so, with everybody's help, Chris, only seven years old at the time, had been a policeman for a day. When people saw how delighted Chris was when his dream came true, they decided to try and help other sick children too, and that was the beginning of Make-A-Wish, Sophia explained. The Foundation tries to give children and their families a special, happy time. A Make-A-Wish volunteer visits the families and asks the children what they would wish for if they could have anything in the world. Sophia said the volunteers were important because they were the ones who helped to make the wishes come true. They do this either by providing things that are necessary, or by raising money or helping out in whatever way they can.

People are ruder today because they are rushed and more time poor than ever before, says Patsy Rowe. Manners have fallen off the radar. Due to our strong attraction to electronic equipment it is a wonder more people don't wake up each morning and greet the singing birds with a complaint about the noise. Here are some examples of rudeness. Some people prefer to do almost everything over the internet. To them, dealing with an actual human is like an evolutionary step backward. It feels very slow because humans don't work at 4G speeds. When you have dinner with friends, you will often notice someone paying more attention to his mobile phone. We have programmed ourselves to think that every new message brings life-changing news, so taking calls and checking our texts are more important than talking to the people we are with. What is worse, some people even tend to send anonymous rude messages by email. However, rudeness is never acceptable. Don't assume it's OK to be rude if the person you're in touch with won't recognize you. If you have something awful to say, have the courage to face the person and say it, write a letter or email and sign it, or forget it. Upsetting people with unsigned messages is cruel and disgusting. We shouldn't blame technology for our shortcomings. Technology is here to help us, but we should not allow it to take over our lives. An important step is acknowledging our shortcomings. People spend a lot of time pointing out bad manners but it would be more helpful if we publicly acknowledge good manners when we see them.

Argentina in the late nineteenth century was an exciting place. Around 1870, it was experiencing an economic boom, and the capital, Buenos Aires, attracted many people. Farmers, as well as a flood of foreigners from Spain and Italy, came to Buenos Aires seeking jobs. These jobs didn't pay well, and the people felt lonely and disappointed with their new life in the city. As the unhappy newcomers moved together in the poor parts of the city, the dance known as the tango came into being. At the beginning the tango was a dance of the lower classes. It was danced in the bars and streets. At that time there were many fewer women than men, so if a man didn't want to be left out, his only choice was to dance with another man so that he could attract the attention of the few available women. Gradually, the dance spread into the upper classes of Argentinean society and became more respectable. In Europe at this time, strong interest in dance from around the world was beginning. This interest in international dance was especially evident in Paris. Every kind of dance from ballet to belly dancing could be found on the stages of the Paris theaters. After tango dancers from Argentina arrived in Europe, they began to draw the interest of the public as they performed their exciting dance in cafes. Though not everyone approved of the new dance, saying it was a little too shocking, they did find supporters to make it popular. The popularity of tango continued to grow in many other parts of the world. Soldiers who returned to the United States from World War I brought the tango to North America. It reached Japan in 1926, and in 2003 the Argentinean embassy in Seoul hired a local tango dancer to act as a kind of dance ambassador, and promote tango throughout South Korea.

items.promptZh: 根据文章 A 回答第 56 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 约三分之一的美国老年人每天只刷一次牙。
explanation.ruleZh: 细节题应直接定位调查结果。

evidence.quote: 33% of seniors brush their teeth only once a day

options.text: Most of them have good habits.
Nearly 30% of them bathe three days a week.
All of them are fighting germs better than expected.
About one third of them brush their teeth only once a day.

items.promptZh: 根据文章 A 回答第 57 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 建议每天至少刷牙两次。
explanation.ruleZh: 数字细节题需区分调查现状与专家建议。

evidence.quote: at least twice a day

options.text: twice a day
three times a day
four times a day
eight times a day

items.promptZh: 根据文章 A 回答第 58 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 文章指出厨房海绵携带的细菌可能比其他物品更多。
explanation.ruleZh: 判断题要逐项核对原文信息。

evidence.quote: your kitchen sponge that can carry more germs than anything else

options.text: We should keep from touching our faces.
There are less than 300 types of bacteria in the mouth.
A kitchen sponge can carry more germs than a toilet.
We should wash our hands before touching a door handle.

items.promptZh: 根据文章 A 回答第 59 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 文章采用调查结果和专家建议的科普杂志风格。
explanation.ruleZh: 判断文章出处时结合标题、数据和面向公众的健康建议。

evidence.quote: The Healthy Habits Survey

options.text: a guide book
a popular magazine
a book review
an official document

items.promptZh: 根据文章 B 回答第 60 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 铺设道路和停车场会减少雨水渗入地下，从而减少地下水。
explanation.ruleZh: 因果题要定位 paved roads、water flow 和 groundwater 的关系。

evidence.quote: The more roads and parking lots we pave

options.text: Using river water.
Throwing batteries away.
Paving parking lots.
Throwing rubbish into lakes.

items.promptZh: 根据文章 B 回答第 61 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 文章说明满足用水需要需要付出很大努力，也需要合理管理。
explanation.ruleZh: 推断题需综合用水量、气候和管理三处信息。

evidence.quote: good management can help to make sure there is enough water

options.text: All water shortages are due to human behavior.
It takes a lot of effort to meet our water needs.
There is much we can do to reduce family size.
The average family in America makes proper use of water.

items.promptZh: 根据文章 B 回答第 62 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 最后一段通过家庭场景给出节约用水的具体建议。
explanation.ruleZh: 段落作用题要概括多个例子共同服务的目的。

evidence.quote: You can take steps to save water in your home

options.text: show us how to fix leaks at home
tell us how to run a dishwasher
prove what drinking glass is best for us
suggest what we can do to save water at home

items.promptZh: 根据文章 B 回答第 63 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 文章重点说明人类活动如何以明显和不明显的方式影响供水。
explanation.ruleZh: 主旨题要覆盖道路铺设、用水管理和家庭节水建议。

evidence.quote: put our water supply in danger

options.text: why paving roads reduces water
how much we depend on water to live
why droughts occur more in dry climates
how human activity affects our water supply

items.promptZh: 根据文章 C 回答第 64 题。

explanation.summaryZh: Sophia 的好朋友曾从 Make-A-Wish 中受益，所以她了解到这个组织。
explanation.ruleZh: 细节题要定位人物了解信息的直接原因。

evidence.quote: helped to make a dream come true for one of her best friends

options.text: benefited from it
volunteered to help it
dreamed about it
told the author about it

items.promptZh: 根据文章 C 回答第 65 题。

explanation.summaryZh: Make-A-Wish 是 1980 年在美国成立的世界性组织，即国际慈善机构。
explanation.ruleZh: 机构信息题要结合 founded、worldwide 和 charity 等关键词。

evidence.quote: a worldwide organization that started in the United States in 1980

options.text: is an international charity
was understood by nobody at first
raises money for poor families
started by drawing the interest of the public

items.promptZh: 根据文章 C 回答第 66 题。

explanation.summaryZh: Chris 的愿望实现后，人们决定帮助其他生病的孩子，这促成了 Make-A-Wish 的开始。
explanation.ruleZh: 事件作用题要关注 Chris 的经历如何推动后续组织成立。

evidence.quote: that was the beginning of Make-A-Wish

options.text: He has been a policeman since he was seven.
He gave people the idea of starting Make-A-Wish.
He wanted people to help make his dream come true.
He was the first child Make-A-Wish helped after it had been set up.

items.promptZh: 根据文章 C 回答第 67 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 志愿者通过提供物品、筹款或其他帮助，让孩子的愿望实现。
explanation.ruleZh: 判断题要以志愿者职责的明确说明为依据。

evidence.quote: the ones who helped to make the wishes come true

options.text: They are important for making wishes come true.
They try to help children get over their illnesses.
They visit sick children to make them feel special.
They provide what is necessary to make Make-A-Wish popular.

items.promptZh: 根据文章 D 回答第 68 题。

explanation.summaryZh: Manners have fallen off the radar 意味着人们越来越少关注自己的礼貌行为。
explanation.ruleZh: 隐含意义题要结合上下文关于粗鲁行为的例子判断。

evidence.quote: Manners have fallen off the radar

options.text: People can tell good from bad behavior.
Radar is able to observe human behavior.
People care little about their behavior.
Radar can predict human behavior.

items.promptZh: 根据文章 D 回答第 69 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 过度依赖网络和电子设备使一些人变得不耐烦，不愿与真实的人打交道。
explanation.ruleZh: 原因题要结合 internet、4G speeds 和 dinner with friends 的语境。

evidence.quote: dealing with an actual human is like an evolutionary step backward

options.text: they are becoming less patient
they are growing too independent
they have to handle many important messages
they have to follow an evolutionary step backward

items.promptZh: 根据文章 D 回答第 70 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 作者称未署名的粗鲁信息令人残酷且恶心，选项 disgusting 与原文一致。
explanation.ruleZh: 态度和词义题要抓住作者的评价词。

evidence.quote: cruel and disgusting

options.text: ridiculous
disgusting
acceptable
reasonable

items.promptZh: 根据文章 D 回答第 71 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 作者认为不应只指出坏习惯，还应在看到好礼貌时公开认可。
explanation.ruleZh: 段落主旨题要概括结尾提出的改进方向。

evidence.quote: publicly acknowledge good manners

options.text: We should applaud good behavior.
Technology can never be blamed.
We should keep pointing out mistakes.
Technology will take over our lives one day.

items.promptZh: 根据文章 E 回答第 72 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 探戈诞生于布宜诺斯艾利斯的贫困地区，文章把它与阿根廷首都联系起来。
explanation.ruleZh: 来源题要结合城市、移民和舞蹈诞生的叙述。

evidence.quote: the capital, Buenos Aires, attracted many people

options.text: belly dancers
American soldiers
a Spanish city
the capital of Argentina

items.promptZh: 根据文章 E 回答第 73 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 探戈最初女性少于男性，男性有时只能与另一名男性跳舞，因此 C 正确。
explanation.ruleZh: 判断题要回到探戈早期社会背景和舞蹈方式的说明。

evidence.quote: his only choice was to dance with another man

options.text: It was created by foreigners from Spain and Italy.
People of the upper classes loved the tango most.
It was often danced by two males in the beginning.
A dancer in Seoul became the Argentinean ambassador.

items.promptZh: 根据文章 E 回答第 74 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 阿根廷探戈舞者到达欧洲后在巴黎咖啡馆表演，说明一战前已传到法国。
explanation.ruleZh: 时间顺序题要根据 Europe、Paris 和 World War I 的先后判断。

evidence.quote: This interest in international dance was especially evident in Paris

options.text: America
Japan
France
South Korea

items.promptZh: 根据文章 E 回答第 75 题。

explanation.summaryZh: 文章按时间顺序介绍探戈的起源、阶层变化和世界传播史。
explanation.ruleZh: 标题题要覆盖起源、发展和传播，而不是只概括一个舞步或地区。

evidence.quote: The popularity of tango continued to grow

options.text: How to Dance the Tango
The History of the Tango
How to Promote the Tango
The Modern Tango Boom
